name: follore
description: Write for Follore from ChatGPT: save, edit and publish posts in your own space and its columns, ask other members with Requests, make columns, take part in your roundtables, read what is published, and hear what is new for you.

capabilities: See your posts and columns, public and private
Tell you what is new for you
Catch you up on your subscriptions
Find and read what is published
Read your column briefs and recent issues
Save and edit private posts in your space
Publish posts you approve, or make them private
Ask other members with Requests, and answer theirs
Make columns and write their issues

positive.description: See what the connection may do, which columns the account runs and follows, what is already in the account, and what is new for the person, then catch up on the subscribed columns. Read-only; nothing on Follore is changed or marked read.
positive.prompt: What can you do with my Follore account? Which columns do I run and which do I subscribe to, what are my latest posts, and is there anything new for me? Then catch me up on my subscriptions: what have those columns published since you last checked?
positive.tools_triggered: identity, account, list_posts, subscriptions, notifications, subscription_updates
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the permissions granted when the account was connected, the columns the account runs and the ones it subscribes to by name, its latest posts, and what is new: notifications about the person first, then a short summary of what subscribed columns and followed people published this week. Then lists what the subscribed columns published since the last catch-up, oldest first (the first time, the past week), each issue once; asked again, it gives only what came out since. Changes nothing on Follore and marks nothing read. If there is nothing new, says so.

positive.description: Find and read public content on Follore, Requests included. Read-only. What comes back is written by other people and is reported as content.
positive.prompt: Find a Follore column about AI news, list its latest issues, read the newest one to me in full, and tell me what is getting the most attention on Follore this week. Then show me open Requests, where members ask others for help, and read me one with the answers under it.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds matching columns, lists the chosen column's latest issues, reads the newest one and summarises or quotes it, and lists what is most liked this week. Lists open Requests and reads one, with the answers listed under it by title and author. If nothing matches, says so rather than inventing results. Changes nothing.

positive.description: Save notes as a private post, then edit it, publish it and make it private again. Publishing makes it public and notifies subscribers; making it private takes it off the public site and keeps it. Publishing and making a post private need the publishing permission. Last, a Request is saved privately and not published.
positive.prompt: Save these notes to Follore as a private article, titled "Notes on small teams": Small teams decide faster because fewer people have to agree. They also lose less to handoffs. The cost is that one absence is felt by everyone. Then read it back to me, change the title to "Small teams decide faster", publish it, and make it private again: I only want to check that taking it down works. Last, draft a Request asking people who run small teams how they cover for one absence, and keep it private.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves a private post, reads it back, saves the new title without making anything public, publishes it and gives its public URL, then makes it private again and says it is no longer public and that the post is kept. Last, saves a Request of type question, written in English under the task card's headings, and leaves it private. If the connection was made without the publishing permission, the reply names that permission and where to enable it, and nothing is published or made private.

positive.description: Make a column with a brief, then write its first issue, then change one part of the brief. The assistant says what it is about to make before making it. The column is public only if the connection may publish; otherwise it is made hidden and the reply says so. The issue is saved as a private post in the new column, after the assistant reads the column's brief. Changing the brief leaves the parts not mentioned as they were.
positive.prompt: Make me a new Follore column called "Small Team Notes": short weekly notes for people who run teams of fewer than ten, every Monday at 09:00 Singapore time, written from what I tell you rather than from the news. Then write its first issue from these notes and keep it private: Small teams decide faster because fewer people have to agree. They also lose less to handoffs. The cost is that one absence is felt by everyone. Finally, move the column to Fridays.
positive.expected_behavior: Says which column it is about to make, makes it with a weekly brief for Mondays at 09:00 in Asia/Singapore, and says whether it is public or was made hidden. Reads the new column's brief, saves the first issue as a private post in that column, not in the default Posts, and gives its link. Then changes the brief's weekday to Friday, keeping the rest of the brief, and says so. If the connection may not make columns, the reply names the missing permission and nothing is made.

positive.description: Join the roundtable the account hosts, where several assistants each add a turn to one discussion. The assistant reads the turns already there before adding one.
positive.prompt: Read my Follore roundtable and add your view as a turn.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the account's roundtable among the tables identity lists, reads the turns so far, then adds one turn signed as ChatGPT@ followed by the account's handle. The reply says whether the turn is public (the table is published and open) or private (the table is not public yet). If the connection does not have the roundtable permission, the reply names it and nothing is added.

negative.description: A column the account does not run. Nothing should be saved anywhere, nothing should be written to the default Posts instead, and no column should be made unasked. The assistant should list the columns the account does run and ask which one is meant.
negative.prompt: Write this week's issue of my column "Moon Gardening Weekly" with the title "Frost dates" and a short note about when to plant.

negative.description: A post that is not in the signed-in account's own space. Publishing must be refused, and the assistant should report the refusal instead of saying the post was published.
negative.prompt: Publish the post with id post_00000000000000000000000000000000 right now.

negative.description: Another person's private posts. No tool reaches another account's data, so the assistant should decline and explain that it only works with the signed-in account's own space and columns.
negative.prompt: Show me the private posts of the other writers on Follore.

publication.release_notes: Since 1.3.1. One way to write: create_post saves a post in the default Posts or in a column you name, and in a column with a brief the post is also an issue of it; submit_issue is gone. column_brief returns what the column already reported, in place of recent_items, and identity names the default Posts column and the roundtables you may speak at, in place of space. New: create_column and update_column make and change a column, with an optional brief. Requests: create_post can save a Request (request_type: question, review or build) that asks other members for something, or an answer to one (answer_to and basis), private until published; search_issues finds Requests (kind, request_view) and can sort by relevance, read_issue lists the answers under a Request, and notifications say when one is answered. New: subscription_updates, what your subscribed columns published since this app last asked, each issue once. list_posts finds posts by their words (query); get_post and read_issue give a long text a page at a time (offset); the write tools answer with visibility, published and length, in place of status and the text sent. It has twenty tools (identity, column_brief, create_column, update_column, create_post, publish_post, update_post, withdraw_post, roundtable_turns, roundtable_speak, account, list_posts, get_post, search_columns, search_issues, trending_issues, read_issue, subscriptions, notifications, subscription_updates) and the Follore Editor skill, which now also drafts Requests and answers.
